cards.title: Excluding the Arrogant 'Until the Camel Passes Through the Eye of the Needle'
cards.note: Surah 7:40 declares that those who reject God's signs will not enter the Garden 'until the camel passes through the eye of the needle,' reproducing Jesus' proverb in Matthew 19:24 and Luke 18:25 alongside its Talmudic counterpart in Berakhot 55b.

discussion.view: Classical commentators explain this clause as a vivid Arabic proverb illustrating an impossibility, or as a shared truth spoken by earlier prophets.
discussion.reply: In the Synoptic Gospels (Matthew 19:24; Luke 18:25), Jesus coins the image of a camel passing through the eye of a needle regarding entry into the kingdom of God, while the Babylonian Talmud (Berakhot 55b) adapts it to an elephant; Surah 7:40 places the Gospel wording directly into divine speech.

cards.quranEn: Surely those who call Our signs a lie, and are arrogant about it – the gates of the sky will not be opened for them, nor will they enter the Garden, until the camel passes through the eye of the needle. In this way We repay the sinners.
quranHighlights: nor will they enter the Garden, until the camel passes through the eye of the needle.

sources.title: Gospel of Matthew (NASB)

highlights: it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.

cards.title: 'If All the Trees on the Earth Were Pens and the Sea Were Ink'
cards.note: Surah 31:27 declares that 'if all the trees on the earth were pens, and the sea were ink—and extending it were seven seas after it—the words of God would still not give out,' matching the rabbinic formula in Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:3 and Shabbat 11a.

discussion.view: Ibn Kathīr and al-Ṭabarī cite reports that this verse was revealed in response to Jewish interlocutors discussing the inexhaustible wisdom of the Torah, affirming that God's words surpass all created bounds.
discussion.reply: In Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:3 and Talmud Bavli Shabbat 11a, Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua use the exact compound hyperbole ('If all the seas were ink, and the reeds in the swamps were quills... they would not suffice to write the matters of Torah'); Surah 31:27 places this rabbinic schoolroom saying directly into the mouth of God.

cards.quranEn: Even if all the trees on the earth were pens, and the sea (were ink) – (and) extending it (were) seven seas after it – the words of God would (still) not give out. God is mighty, wise.
quranHighlights: Even if all the trees on the earth were pens, and the sea (were ink) – (and) extending it (were) seven seas after it – the words of God would (still) not give out.

sources.title: Midrash Shir HaShirim Rabbah
sources.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: If all the seas were ink, [all the reeds that grow in] the swamps were quills, the heavens and the earth were scrolls, and all people were scribes, they would not suffice to write the matters of Torah that I have learned [from my teachers], and I culled only the equivalent of one who dips the tip of his quill, like a brush, in the sea. Rabbi Yehoshua says: If all the seas were ink, the swamps were quills, the heavens and the earth were sheets of parchment, and all people were scribes, they would not suffice to write the matters of Torah that I have learned, and I culled only the equivalent of one who dips the tip of his quill, like a brush, in the sea.
highlights: If all the seas were ink, [all the reeds that grow in] the swamps were quills, the heavens and the earth were scrolls, and all people were scribes, they would not suffice to write the matters of Torah
sources.orig: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, אִם יִהְיוּ כָּל הַיַּמִּים דְּיוֹ, וַאֲגַמִּים קוּלְמוֹסִין, וְשָׁמַיִם וְאֶרֶץ מְגִלּוֹת, וְכָל בְּנֵי הָאָדָם לַבְלָרִים, אֵין מַסְפִּיקִין לִכְתּוֹב [דברי תורה שלמדתי], וַאֲנִי לֹא חִסַּרְתִּיהָ אֶלָּא כְּאָדָם שֶׁמַּטְבִּיל זַכְרוּתוֹ כְּמִכְּחוֹל בַּיָּם. רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר אִם יִהְיוּ כָּל הַיַּמִּים דְּיוֹ, וַאֲגַמִּים קוּלְמוֹסִין, וְשָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ יְרִיעוֹת, וְכָל בְּנֵי אָדָם לַבְלָרִין, אֵין מַסְפִּיקִין לִכְתּוֹב דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁלָּמַדְתִּי, וְלֹא חִסַּרְתִּיהָ רַק כְּאָדָם שֶׁמַּטְבִּיל זַכְרוּתוֹ כְּמִכְּחוֹל בַּיָּם.

sources.title: Talmud Bavli, Tractate Shabbat
sources.en: Even if all the seas would be ink, and the reeds that grow near swamps would be quills, and the heavens would be parchment upon which the words would be written, and all the people would be scribes; all of these are insufficient to write the unquantifiable space of governmental authority, i.e., all the considerations with which a government must concern itself and deal. Rav Mesharshiya said: What is the verse that alludes to this? “The Heavens on High and the land to the depth and the heart of kings are unsearchable” (Proverbs 25:3).
highlights: Even if all the seas would be ink, and the reeds that grow near swamps would be quills, and the heavens would be parchment upon which the words would be written, and all the people would be scribes; all of these are insufficient to write

cards.title: Creating the World in Six Days and 'No Weariness Touched Us'
cards.note: Surah 50:38 states that God created the heavens and earth in six days and adds 'No weariness touched Us in doing that,' matching Bereishit Rabbah 10:9 ('It was not with toil and not with exertion that the Holy One created His world') and Isaiah 40:28.

discussion.view: al-Ṭabarī and Ibn Kathīr report that Surah 50:38 was revealed to refute a Jewish claim that God rested on the seventh day to recover from fatigue.
discussion.reply: While Genesis 2:2 and Exodus 31:17 state that God 'ceased and rested' on the seventh day, neither the Hebrew Bible nor rabbinic tradition teaches that God experienced fatigue: Isaiah 40:28 explicitly states that the Creator 'shall not hunger, nor be weary,' and Bereishit Rabbah 10:9 explains Genesis 2:2 in the exact terms echoed by Surah 50:38 ('It was not with toil and not with exertion that the Holy One blessed be He created His world').

cards.quranEn: Certainly We created the heavens and the earth, and whatever is between them, in six days. No weariness touched Us in (doing) that.
quranHighlights: We created the heavens and the earth, and whatever is between them, in six days. No weariness touched Us in (doing) that.

cards.title: Parable of the Deep-Rooted Fruitful Tree vs. the Tree Uprooted From the Earth
cards.note: Surah 14:24–26 contrasts a good tree with firm root yielding fruit every season with a bad tree uprooted from the earth, matching Rabbi Eleazar ben Azariah's parable in Mishnah Pirkei Avot 3:17 of the deep-rooted tree versus the wind-uprooted tree.

discussion.view: Classical exegetes interpret this passage as a divine parable likening the testimony of faith to a deeply rooted date palm and disbelief to a rootless colocynth plant.
discussion.reply: While Psalm 1:3 supplies the clause 'which shall yield its fruit in its season,' the specific contrast between a tree with firm roots that stands unshaken and a counterpart with weak roots that is 'uprooted from the earth' reproduces Rabbi Eleazar ben Azariah's parable in Mishnah Pirkei Avot 3:17.

cards.quranEn: [24] Do you not see how God has struck a parable? A good word is like a good tree. Its root is firm and its branch (reaches) to the sky, [25] giving its fruit every season by the permission of its Lord. God strikes parables for the people so that they may take heed. [26] But the parable of a bad word is like a bad tree, uprooted from the earth, without any support for it.
quranHighlights: A good word is like a good tree. Its root is firm and its branch (reaches) to the sky,
like a bad tree, uprooted from the earth, without any support for it.

sources.title: Mishnah Pirkei Avot 3:17
sources.ref: Pirkei Avot 3:17 (Rabbi Eleazar ben Azariah's Parable of the Uprooted Tree with Few Roots vs. the Firm Tree with Many Roots)
sources.en: He used to say: one whose wisdom exceeds his deeds, to what may he be compared? To a tree whose branches are numerous but whose roots are few, so that when the wind comes, it uproots it and overturns it, as it is said, “He shall be like a bush in the desert, which does not sense the coming of good. It is set in the scorched places of the wilderness, in a barren land without inhabitant” (Jeremiah 17:6). But one whose deeds exceed his wisdom, to what may he be compared? To a tree whose branches are few but roots are many, so that even if all the winds in the world come and blow upon it, they cannot move it out of its place, as it is said, “He shall be like a tree planted by waters, sending forth its roots by a stream. It does not sense the coming of heat, its leaves are ever fresh. It has no care in a year of drought; it does not cease to yield fruit” (ibid, 17:8).
highlights: To a tree whose branches are numerous but whose roots are few, so that when the wind comes, it uproots it and overturns it

cards.title: People of the Book Saying: 'The Fire Will Touch Us for a Number of Days'
cards.note: Surah 3:24 quotes People of the Book saying 'The Fire will touch us for a number of days,' matching the rabbinic doctrine codified in Mishnah Eduyot 2:10 that 'the judgment of the wicked in Gehinnom continues twelve months.'

discussion.view: al-Ṭabarī and Ibn Kathīr note that Surah 3:24 quotes the claim of Medinan Jews who held that their punishment in the Fire would last for a fixed, limited duration.
discussion.reply: The verse accurately reflects the rabbinic tradition preserved in Mishnah Eduyot 2:10 (compiled c. AD 200), in which Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Yohanan ben Nuri define the judgment of the wicked in Gehinnom as lasting either twelve months or from Passover to Shavuot.

cards.quranEn: That is because they said, ‘The Fire will only touch us for a number of days.’ What they forged has deceived them in their religion.
quranHighlights: they said, ‘The Fire will only touch us for a number of days.’

sources.title: Mishnah Eduyot
sources.en: The judgment of the wicked in gehinom [continues] twelve months, for it is said, and “It will be from one month until its [same] month” (Isaiah 66:23). Rabbi Yohanan ben Nuri says: “[As long as] from Passover to Shavuoth, for it is said, “And from one Sabbath until its [next] Sabbath” (ibid.).
highlights: The judgment of the wicked in gehinom [continues] twelve months
[As long as] from Passover to Shavuoth

cards.title: Jews and Christians Saying: 'We Are the Sons of God, and His Beloved'
cards.note: Surah 5:18 quotes Jews and Christians saying 'We are the sons of God, and His beloved,' matching Rabbi Akiva's saying in Pirkei Avot 3:14 ('Beloved are Israel in that they were called children to the All-Present') and 1 John 3:1.

discussion.view: Commentators explain that Surah 5:18 records and rejects the verbal boast of seventh-century Jewish and Christian communities claiming special filial standing before God.
discussion.reply: While Deuteronomy 14:1 and 1 John 3:1 call believers 'children of God,' the specific pairing of the two predicates ('sons of God, and His beloved') reproduces Rabbi Akiva's famous saying in Mishnah Pirkei Avot 3:14 ('Beloved are Israel in that they were called children to the All-Present') and treats a metaphor of covenantal love as a literal claim to exemption from divine chastisement.

cards.quranEn: The Jews and the Christians say, ‘We are the sons of God, and His beloved.’ Say: ‘Then why does He punish you for your sins? No! You are human beings, (part) of what He created. He forgives whomever He pleases and He punishes whomever He pleases. To God (belongs) the kingdom of the heavens and the earth, and whatever is between them. To Him is the (final) destination.’
quranHighlights: The Jews and the Christians say, ‘We are the sons of God, and His beloved.’

sources.title: Pirkei Avot
sources.en: Beloved are Israel in that they were called children to the All-Present. Especially beloved are they for it was made known to them that they are called children of the All-Present, as it is said: “you are children to the Lord your God” (Deuteronomy 14:1).
highlights: Beloved are Israel in that they were called children to the All-Present.
you are children to the Lord your God

cards.quranAr: وَقَالَتِ ٱلۡيَهُودُ وَٱلنَّصَٰرَىٰ نَحۡنُ أَبۡنَـٰٓؤُاْ ٱللَّهِ وَأَحِبَّـٰٓؤُهُۥۚ قُلۡ فَلِمَ يُعَذِّبُكُم بِذُنُوبِكُمۖ بَلۡ أَنتُم بَشَرٞ مِّمَّنۡ خَلَقَۚ يَغۡفِرُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيُعَذِّبُ مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَلِلَّهِ مُلۡكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا بَيۡنَهُمَاۖ وَإِلَيۡهِ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ

cards.title: Sinai Covenant Inversion: 'We Hear and Disobey' vs. 'We Will Hear, and Do'
cards.note: Surah 2:93 reports the Israelites answering at Sinai 'We hear and disobey,' inverting the biblical Sinai covenant pledge 'We will hear, and do' in Deuteronomy 5:27 and its celebration in Talmud Bavli Shabbat 88a.

discussion.view: Classical commentators explain that while the Israelites spoke obedience with their tongues at Sinai, their rebellious hearts inwardly replied 'We hear and disobey.'
discussion.reply: In Deuteronomy 5:27, Israel pledges at Sinai 'we will hear, and do' (Hebrew shamaʿnu we-ʿasinu), a phrase celebrated in Talmud Bavli Shabbat 88a; because the Hebrew verb ʿasinu ('we will do') sounds like the Arabic verb ʿaṣaynā ('we disobey'), Surah 2:93 turns the Torah's vow of obedience into a declaration of defiance ('We hear and disobey').

cards.quranEn: And when We took a covenant with you, and raised the mountain above you: ‘Hold fast what We have given you, and hear,’ they said, ‘We hear and disobey.’ And they were made to drink the calf in their hearts because of their disbelief. Say: ‘Evil is what your belief commands you, if you are believers.’
quranHighlights: And when We took a covenant with you, and raised the mountain above you: ‘Hold fast what We have given you, and hear,’ they said, ‘We hear and disobey.’

sources.title: Book of Deuteronomy (LXX / Torah)
sources.en: Do you draw near, and hear all that the Lord our God shall say, and you shall speak to us all things whatever the Lord our God shall speak to you, and we will hear, and do.
highlights: and we will hear, and do.

sources.title: Babylonian Talmud, Shabbat 88a
sources.en: Rabbi Simai taught: When Israel accorded precedence to the declaration “We will do” over the declaration “We will hear,” 600,000 ministering angels came and tied two crowns to each and every member of the Jewish people, one corresponding to “We will do” and one corresponding to “We will hear.” And when the people sinned with the Golden Calf, 1,200,000 angels of destruction descended and removed them from the people, as it is stated in the wake of the sin of the Golden Calf: “And the children of Israel stripped themselves of their ornaments from Mount Horeb onward” (Exodus 33:6).
highlights: When Israel accorded precedence to the declaration “We will do” over the declaration “We will hear,”
one corresponding to “We will do” and one corresponding to “We will hear.”
sources.orig: דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי סִימַאי: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁהִקְדִּימוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל ״נַעֲשֶׂה״ לְ״נִשְׁמָע״ בָּאוּ שִׁשִּׁים רִיבּוֹא שֶׁל מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת, לְכׇל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל קָשְׁרוּ לוֹ שְׁנֵי כְתָרִים, אֶחָד כְּנֶגֶד ״נַעֲשֶׂה״ וְאֶחָד כְּנֶגֶד ״נִשְׁמָע״. וְכֵיוָן שֶׁחָטְאוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל, יָרְדוּ מֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים רִיבּוֹא מַלְאֲכֵי חַבָּלָה וּפֵירְקוּם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיִּתְנַצְּלוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת עֶדְיָם מֵהַר חוֹרֵב״.

cards.quranAr: وَإِذۡ أَخَذۡنَا مِيثَٰقَكُمۡ وَرَفَعۡنَا فَوۡقَكُمُ ٱلطُّورَ خُذُواْ مَآ ءَاتَيۡنَٰكُم بِقُوَّةٖ وَٱسۡمَعُواْۖ قَالُواْ سَمِعۡنَا وَعَصَيۡنَا وَأُشۡرِبُواْ فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ ٱلۡعِجۡلَ بِكُفۡرِهِمۡۚ قُلۡ بِئۡسَمَا يَأۡمُرُكُم بِهِۦٓ إِيمَٰنُكُمۡ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ

cards.title: 'If the Sea Were Ink for the Words of My Lord, the Sea Would Give Out'
cards.note: Surah 18:109 states 'If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would indeed give out before the words of my Lord would give out,' matching Rabbi Eliezer's formula in Midrash Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:3.

discussion.view: Muslim exegetes view this verse as a divine command instructing the Prophet to illustrate the infinite scope of God's knowledge to his questioners.
discussion.reply: As in Surah 31:27, this verse adapts the rabbinic hyperbole preserved in Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:3 and Talmud Bavli Shabbat 11a ('If all the seas were ink... they would not suffice to write the matters of Torah that I have learned'), elevating a rabbinic tribute to Torah scholarship into direct divine speech.

cards.quranEn: Say: ‘If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would indeed give out before the words of my Lord would give out, even if We brought (another sea) like it as an extension.’
quranHighlights: ‘If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would indeed give out before the words of my Lord would give out, even if We brought (another sea) like it as an extension.’

sources.title: Midrash Shir HaShirim Rabbah
sources.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: If all the seas were ink, [all the reeds that grow in] the swamps were quills, the heavens and the earth were scrolls, and all people were scribes, they would not suffice to write the matters of Torah that I have learned [from my teachers], and I culled only the equivalent of one who dips the tip of his quill, like a brush, in the sea.
highlights: If all the seas were ink, [all the reeds that grow in] the swamps were quills, the heavens and the earth were scrolls, and all people were scribes, they would not suffice to write the matters of Torah
sources.orig: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, אִם יִהְיוּ כָּל הַיַּמִּים דְּיוֹ, וַאֲגַמִּים קוּלְמוֹסִין, וְשָׁמַיִם וְאֶרֶץ מְגִלּוֹת, וְכָל בְּנֵי הָאָדָם לַבְלָרִים, אֵין מַסְפִּיקִין לִכְתּוֹב [דברי תורה שלמדתי], וַאֲנִי לֹא חִסַּרְתִּיהָ אֶלָּא כְּאָדָם שֶׁמַּטְבִּיל זַכְרוּתוֹ כְּמִכְּחוֹל בַּיָּם.
